articles.title: Hull's deal for Frankfurt winger Bahoya falls through
articles.summary: Hull City's move for Eintracht Frankfurt winger Jean-Matteo Bahoya falls through after the player decides against joining the Premier League side.
body: Hull City have agreed a deal with Eintracht Frankfurt to sign winger Jean-Matteo Bahoya.
The 21-year-old is understood to be open to the move and has been granted permission to undergo a medical in East Yorkshire before Tuesday's transfer deadline.

The France Under-21 international, who has previously been linked with several Premier League clubs, has seven goals and eight assists in 78 matches for Frankfurt since joining from French club Angers in 2024.
Primarily a left winger, he is capable of playing in multiple attacking positions and holds the Bundesliga speed record after being clocked at 23.09mph during a match against Bochum in 2025.

articles.title: Chelsea hold off Brighton in 4-3 win but remain chaotic under Xabi Alonso
articles.summary: In the fullness of time Chelsea’s surrender against Brighton & Hove Albion last April may come to be seen as the turning point. The humiliation accelerated Liam Rosenior’s demise and forced the Stamford Bridge hierarchy into a reckoning which has led to the appointment of Xabi Alonso, a shift in…
body: For now, though, the argument that Emiliano Martínez is the final piece in the jigsaw seems a touch premature. There are many enjoyable parts to Alonso’s rejigged Chelsea, especially when Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and João Pedro click in attack, but other problems remain and the early evidence suggests a title challenge will only be sustained if performances become less chaotic.

Alonso looked ready to erupt when Chelsea found themselves clinging on to their lead midway through the second half. His side had made a blistering start to this game, rattling three unanswered goals past a weakened Brighton, but the level dipped. Anxiety gripped Stamford Bridge for a while and although Palmer took over during the dying stages, cutting inside to make it 4-2 with a beautiful finish, there is a sense that Chelsea’s winning start to the Alonso era has been a bit too fun.

Conceding five goals in their first two league games is not good enough. Martínez played well but was denied a clean sheet on his debut after joining from Aston Villa for £7.5m. Brighton exposed shortcomings in the system and Alonso will want more control.

articles.title: Ireland end World Championships with two silvers
articles.summary: Ireland brought the 2026 World Rowing Championships to a close with two silver medals on the final day of racing at the Bosbaan in Amsterdam.
body: Belfast’s Konan Pazzaia and partner Margaret Cremen were second in the mixed doubles sculls behind the Netherlands.
It was Cremen’s second medal of the championships after her thrilling victory with Zoe Hyde in the women’s double sculls on Friday.
Fiona Murtagh put up a stout defence of her world single sculls title but was beaten to gold by Great Britain’s Lauren Henry, in what was a reversal of last year’s result.
After coming third in the semi-finals of the double sculls earlier on Sunday, Cremen and Pazzaia delivered another excellent performance to claim the silver medal.

articles.title: Golden Tempo's Travers loss to Leading Change the latest in Saratoga's legacy of upsets
articles.summary: The Saratoga race track is famed as the 'Graveyard of Champions.' Saturday, another superstar lost there when Golden Tempo was third in the Travers.
body: SARATOGA SPRINGS - Chalk up another one who fell to the "Graveyard of Champions."

Saratoga Race Course has long been known as the track where some of horse racing's greatest legends suffered their most surprising losses. Saturday, another superstar was defeated at the Spa, as Kentucky Derby and Belmont Stakes winner Golden Tempo could only muster a late-closing third in a Travers Stakes won by the inexperienced Leading Change, who was making just his third career start.
After winning the Derby and Belmont with similar late runs, Golden Tempo lingered at the back of the pack early in the Travers in company with his familiar rival, Renegade.

But unlike during the Triple Crown season, on Saturday the speed horses were able to hang on at the front of the field. Frontrunner Napoleon Solo held the lead deep into the stretch until the Brad Cox-trained Leading Change, who sat second throughout the race under jockey Manny Franco, made his final surge to win by a half-length.

articles.title: Barcelona close to deal for Arsenal's Jesus
articles.summary: Barcelona are closing in on a move for Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus in a deal worth £8.6m.
body: Barcelona are closing in on a move for Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus worth £8.6m (10m euros).
A deal for the Brazil international is believed to be at an advanced stage and, while the finer details still require finalising, the transfer is expected to be completed before Tuesday's deadline.
Napoli had shown an interest in Jesus, but the 29-year-old is set to join last season's Spanish league champions and will travel for a medical on Monday.
Jesus joined Arsenal from Manchester City in 2022, scoring 32 goals and adding 22 assists in 123 appearances for the Gunners.

articles.title: What time is NFL 53-man roster cut deadline?
articles.summary: NFL teams have the important task of finalizing their rosters for the 2026 season, and that deadline is quickly approaching with just two weeks remaining until kickoff.
body: All 32 franchises currently have a host of players battling to make squads, but the reality is not everyone will make that final cut. Head coaches face the difficult task of trimming rosters before the season begins Sept. 9.

The reigning champion Seattle Seahawks open up their title defense against the New England Patriots in a Super Bowl rematch. Meanwhile, the NFL heads to Australia for its first-ever game on the continent the following day.

However, fans are closely watching which players won’t be involved in each team’s 53-man rosters for the upcoming season. The Big Lead is keeping track of all major cuts heading into the upcoming deadline.

Every active squad must be trimmed down to 53 players on Aug. 30 at the NFL’s 6 p.m. ET deadline. That important decision for coaches and general managers comes two Sundays before the league opens back up for play.

articles.title: Colts announce trade with Bills for much needed backup center
articles.summary: On Sunday morning, the Indianapolis Colts announced a trade with the Buffalo Bills, in which the Colts will send 2027 6th round pick and receive Bills backup center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger and a 2027 7th round pick: 🚨TRADE🚨 we have acquired C Sedrick Van Pran-Granger and a 2027 seventh-round…
body: This is one, where at the very least, everyone reasonably expected Indianapolis to be very active on the league waiver wire regarding final cuts, looking for a competent 2nd-string center behind starter Tanor Bortolini.

With Van Pran-Granger likely on the roster bubble with the Bills, the Colts jumped the waive wire order and were able to land a young player, who they believe can be a decent backup center, at a very minimal cost of draft capital for next year.

The need for a backup center only heightened after yesterday, when in Saturday’s preseason finale, Colts transitioning 2nd-string center Dalton Tucker struggled snapping out of shotgun, with several errant snaps. Tucker would figure to transition solely back to backup offensive guard after this latest center acquisition.

Regarding Van Pran-Granger, the former 2024 5th round pick of the Bills stands at 6,’4”, 315 pounds, and was a former First-Team All-SEC and 2x CFP National Champion with the Georgia Bulldogs. Over the past two seasons for Buffalo, he’s appeared in 31 career games, making 2 starts.

articles.summary: Arsenal have agreed a club-record £55.7m fee with Al Hilal to sell Gabriel Martinelli, with a deal also agreed in principle for fellow Brazilian Gabriel Jesus to depart for Barcelona.
body: Martinelli has now been granted permission to have a medical with the Saudi Pro League club and is set to become the biggest sale in Arsenal's history.
His move to Al Hilal will surpass the £40m Arsenal received from Liverpool for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain in the summer of 2017.
Martinelli's compatriot Gabriel Jesus is also set to leave after Arsenal agreed an £8.6m deal in principle with Barcelona.
All sides are now working on the details of the transfer and it is progressing towards a conclusion.

articles.title: PLAYER RATINGS I Paris FC 3-0 Nice: Kebbal and Sinayoko lead Liam Rosenior’s PFC to first home win of the season
articles.summary: Ligue 1 McDonald’s, Matchday 2, 30/08/2026. Paris FC secured their first win of the season following a convincing performance against OGC Nice. Lassine Sinayoko, the Parisians’ star summer signing, scored his first goal for his new club. The Match.
body: It was a match that got off to a lively start, but neither side was able to pose a threat in front of the opposition’s goal. It wasn’t until the twentieth minute of play that Lassine Sinayoko converted a penalty – his first goal for PFC – following a run by Ilan Kebbal that was brought down by Youssouf Ndayishimiye, sending a first wave of excitement through the supporters packed into the stands at the Jean-Bouin Stadium.
The first… and the only one in a relatively lacklustre first half between two sides keen to close down the spaces and prevent their opponents’ counter-attacks.

Although active, the Nice players posed little threat in the first half and began the second with the intention of being more incisive. But it was ultimately the Parisians who struck first, managing to double their lead following a fine move between Kebbal and Samir Chergui, finished off by the latter.

articles.title: McInnes expecting Rangers transfer activity before window closes after Aberdeen win
articles.summary: Derek McInnes has revealed Rangers are expecting to be busy in the final days of the transfer window after securing a much-needed first Scottish Premiership win of the season at Aberdeen.
body: Lawrence Shankland's second-half penalty secured a 1-0 victory at Pittodrie, easing some of the pressure on McInnes after a bruising week which saw Rangers knocked out of Europe by Jablonec.
But the Rangers boss says further business is expected before the window closes, with the club still looking to strengthen in attack and uncertainty remaining over the future of Nico Raskin.
"I think there will be," McInnes said when asked if Rangers would make more signings.
"I still think we're looking to replace Youssef [Chermiti]. It's a few weeks ago now, he went down, and we've been working really hard to try and bring in an added goal at the top end of the pitch.
